factors.verdict: KEEP — weight frozen, do not raise
factors.numbers: Brier on 438 lined player stats: base 0.2812, grades off 0.2812, half 0.2816, doubled 0.2826. Off helped rush attempts (0.2453 → 0.2366, n=33) and hurt receptions (0.2687 → 0.2706, n=142). Doubling was worse in all 6 markets.
factors.why: Net effect is zero within noise on one week. Doubling is clearly worse, so the trench weight stays at 15% of efficiency and is not raised. Run-game trench stays on watch: if rush attempts improve again with it off next week, it gets cut.

factors.factor: Raw sim probability vs the market
factors.numbers: Brier on priced board lines: sim 0.2587 vs no-vig market 0.2519. By market — receptions sim 0.2461 vs market 0.2515 (sim better); rush yds 0.29 vs 0.25; rec yds 0.2561 vs 0.25; pass yds 0.2565 vs 0.2503.
factors.why: Each market now blends the sim toward the no-vig price with a learned weight (shrunk toward 50/50 so one week can't swing it): completions 0.54, pass_att 0.54, pass_td 0.59, pass_yds 0.41, rec_yds 0.33, receptions 0.72, rush_att 0.5, rush_rec_yds 0.3, rush_yds 0.3.

factors.numbers: Board overs went 81-117 (40.9%, -26.87u); unders 86-73 (54.1%, 21.95u). Week 9 overs were also over-predicted (54.6% sim vs 50.0% actual, 212 bets).
factors.why: Two straight weeks of overs landing under the sim. Overs now give back half the measured gap, capped at 4 points.

factors.numbers: Week 10 sim backtest (13 games, 438 lined stats, 3 seeds x 4,000 draws): overall Brier base 0.2817 vs blitz-only 0.2821; QB pass yds 0.2864 → 0.2852 (MAE 83.356 → 83.117); completions 0.3085 → 0.3091; rec yds 0.2901 → 0.2911. Out-of-sample check on 175 QB games (2026 weeks 4–11, rates from earlier weeks only): the QB's blitz split made the forecast worse in every piece — comp% error +2.801%, YPA +1.157%, sack rate +5.751%. A defense's raw blitz rate does correlate with lower QB YPA vs his own baseline (r = -0.157), but the per-QB blitz splits point the wrong way too often.
factors.why: Wired end to end: every defense now carries its 2026 blitz rate and every QB with 40+ dropbacks carries his vs-blitz comp/YPA/sack split, in both the Python engine and the in-app sim. The evidence says the QB blitz splits add noise, so the weight is 0 (learning.json sim_factors.weights.blitz). It's re-tested each review and turns back on if it starts beating the base.

factors.factor: Defensive pressure vs QB under pressure
factors.verdict: KEEP for YPA and sacks (QB split at 50%), ZERO for completions and scrambles
factors.numbers: Week 10 sim backtest: overall Brier base 0.2817 vs pressure-matchup 0.2823, both 0.2826, final setting 0.2821; QB pass yds 0.2864 → 0.285 (final 0.2857, side hit 0.436 → 0.474); completions 0.3085 → 0.3092; QB rush yds 0.2714 → 0.2734. Out-of-sample on 175 QB games: YPA error -0.08% with the QB's own split and -0.193% with league-average sensitivity; sack-rate error -0.12% / -0.242%; comp% got worse (+1.079%) and scrambles got worse (+0.263%). Defense pressure rate vs QB YPA residual r = -0.12; vs sack-rate residual r = 0.072.
factors.why: Each defense's 2026 pressure rate (PFR times_pressured ÷ dropbacks faced) above or below league shifts the QB's pressured share. The change is that extra share times the QB's 2025 pressured-minus-clean gap, blended 50/50 with the league gap, then capped: YPA ±0.30, sack rate ±1.2 pts. Comp% and scramble pieces are zeroed because they made forecasts worse. Effects are small — a few pass yards per QB — and inside seed noise on one sim week (±0.001 Brier), so this stays on probation.

takeaways: Bets of the Night went 2-3: +0.217u at the stakes we published (-0.827u if each were 1u). Watson under and Kyren Williams under cashed; Penix under, Love over and Vele over missed.

Parlays of the Night went 3-4: +0.055u at the published dust stakes, +5.19u at 1u each. Both of the chat-only SF@DAL parlays hit (Flournoy/Pickens overs; Javonte Williams/Purdy unders), but their prices weren't saved, so they're W/L only.

Your 16-leg FanDuel ticket hit 11 of 16 and lost. Misses: Kyren Williams 40+ rush yds (had 23); Josh Allen 200+ pass yds (had 196); Brock Bowers 25+ rec yds (had 18); Jaylen Warren 40+ rush yds (had 15); Derrick Henry 40+ rush yds (had 10).
Full board: 167-190 (46.8%), -4.92u on 275 priced props. The sim's average miss was 18.0 vs 16.58 for the posted line, so the line was the better forecast.
Overs were the leak: 81-117 (40.9%, -26.87u) while unders went 86-73 (+21.95u). Week 9 showed the same tilt.
Confidence was backwards. The 55–60% band hit 37.9% (−24.2u), and the 65%+ band hit 35.6%. The 50–55% band was the profitable one (+16.5u).
Receptions was the only market where the sim beat the market's no-vig price (Brier 0.2461 vs 0.2515). In rushing yards the sim added nothing over the line (0.290 vs 0.250).

Ops miss: on Mon 11/16 and Tue 11/17, the weekday light run re-published the frozen 11/13 data inside the bundle. After the games were final, the hub briefly showed a stale Week 10 board and an old Tyler Higbee Bet of the Night.
Blitz and pressure percentages never reached the sim in Week 10 (0 of 28 team sides carried them). They're wired in now; see the factor verdicts below.

improvements.done: New data/learning.json. Each market's sim probability now blends with the no-vig price: completions 0.54, pass_att 0.54, pass_td 0.59, pass_yds 0.41, rec_yds 0.33, receptions 0.72, rush_att 0.5, rush_rec_yds 0.3, rush_yds 0.3. The War Room packets, the Bet of the Night, the parlays' candidate legs, and the Board's hit % and EV all read it.
Overs give back 3.2 points (half the measured over gap, capped at 4).

Light, publish and War Room runs now pull the live board first if it's newer than the bundle, so a weekday run can't roll the hub back. The War Room brain and log now carry week to week instead of resetting.
Each bot gets a Week 10 lesson from learning.json, and the whys show the raw sim next to the review-adjusted number.
Week picker (Week 10 and Week 9). Week 10 shows the record, units, CLV, every Bet and Parlay of the Night, the ticket, factor verdicts, and calibration.
Trench grades kept at current weight. Blitz % is now wired into both sims with weight 0 after the backtest; defensive pressure vs QB-under-pressure is live for YPA and sacks only, capped.
Each publish now archives the pre-kick board and every published pick (pick-archive file). Once ESPN shows the week final, the next run grades it, refits learning.json and adds the week to this tab.

gaps: Thursday WSH@NYG had no board capture before kickoff (the first Week 10 publish was after it), so its props aren't in the board grade.
CLV uses the last pre-kick capture from our own publishes, not a true closing print. Kyren Williams's Bet of the Night had no later capture before kickoff.
Your FanDuel ticket's price and stake aren't in the data, so it's graded by leg and W/L only, no units.
The two chat-only SF@DAL parlays had no saved price, so they're W/L only.
39 board props were void because the player wasn't in the ESPN box score.
One week of data. Learned weights are shrunk toward 50/50 and get refit after each graded week.
Blitz/pressure backtest: Week 9 has no saved pre-kick sim specs (only Week 10 snapshots exist), so the sim backtest is Week 10 only; the 175 QB-game out-of-sample check covers weeks 4–11.

The pressure definition differs by source: PFR times_pressured (2026 defense rates) vs NGS-style was_pressure (2025 QB splits). Only differences from league and pressured-minus-clean gaps are used, not raw levels.

Ablations ran on the in-app sim (pwa/sim-engine.js, same formulas as hub/nfl_engine.py) at 4,000 draws x 3 seeds per game; base Brier moved 0.2812–0.2822 between seeds, so differences under ~0.001 are noise.
